# frozen_string_literal: true

def slugify(title)
  title
    .unicode_normalize(:nfkd)
    .encode("ASCII", invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "")
    .downcase
    .gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
    .gsub(/\A-+|-+\z/, "")
end

if __FILE__ == $PROGRAM_NAME
  require "minitest/autorun"

  class SlugifyTest < Minitest::Test
    def test_basic
      assert_equal "hello-world", slugify("Hello, World!")
    end

    def test_collapses_whitespace_and_punctuation
      assert_equal "ruby-is-fun", slugify("  Ruby -- is   fun!!  ")
    end

    def test_strips_accents
      assert_equal "cafe-creme", slugify("Café Crème")
    end

    def test_keeps_digits
      assert_equal "top-10-tips", slugify("Top 10 Tips")
    end

    def test_empty
      assert_equal "", slugify("!!!")
    end
  end
end

I added `slugify.rb` with a `slugify` method and tests in the same file. I ran the tests and all 5 pass.

What the method does:
1. Converts accented letters to plain ones ("Café" → "cafe") and drops any other non-ASCII characters.
2. Lowercases the text.
3. Turns each run of anything other than letters and digits into a single hyphen.
4. Removes hyphens from the start and end.

The tests check the "Hello, World!" example, extra spaces and punctuation, accents, digits, and input that's only punctuation (which gives an empty string).

The tests only run when you run the file directly, so you can `require` it elsewhere without them running. To run them: `ruby slugify.rb`.
